notes: Discriminating assertions: the baseline missed the empty alt text and the missing user glossary on the seeded fixture, and the missing exploratory-testing page on the renamed layout; the script catches all three deterministically.

Non-discriminating: verdict present, three books identified, 'both guides' in root README, file paths cited: both configurations pass these every time. They guard against regressions but do not measure skill value.
Report-structure assertions (must-fix vs deviations vs suggestions) fail for the baseline by construction: it cannot know the fixed format. Treat as a consistency check, not a quality signal.

Baseline runs were slower (171s vs 143s mean) with high variance (one run 277s): without the script each agent re-derives link/orphan/SUMMARY checks by hand, mostly with ad-hoc shell loops, and two of three baseline agents ran a full mdBook build on a scratch copy.
Token usage is similar (~62k vs ~60k mean). The skill spends its tokens on the qualitative pass (lead paragraphs, version drift, tone) rather than on structural discovery.
Single run per configuration: variance figures are across evals, not across repeated runs of one eval.

Baseline reports surfaced two ideas worth folding into the skill: cross-book ../book/ links break when each book is a separate GitBook space; and the template itself should be written down in the repo (docs/README.md).
